item.description: Vladimir Putin pitched Donald Trump's son-in-law on a Russian oil deal at the Kremlin last month. The Treasury Department rejected a bid for Lukoil's refineries and gas stations last November, calling the would-be buyer "the Kremlin's puppet." This time the leading bidders include an Emirati royal who is effectively Jared Kushner's business partner, and the US government would take a stake alongside them. Kushner and Steve Witkoff, peace negotiators the Senate never confirmed, helped set the government's terms. Lukoil owns about 200 stations in New York, New Jersey and Pennsylvania. The administration says the sale will lower energy prices for everyday Americans. Diesel just hit the highest price ever recorded and is raising the cost of trucking everything to grocery shelves. item.title: The Billionaire's Tax Loophole That Lets You Borrow Money Without Paying Tax
item.description: The ultra-wealthy have a clever financial strategy known as the "buy, borrow, die" loophole to avoid paying income taxes. First, billionaires purchase massive amounts of appreciating assets like stocks or corporate shares. Instead of selling these assets to get cash, which would trigger capital gains taxes, they use them as collateral for loans. Because the government does not view borrowed money as income, these loans are entirely tax-free. This allows wealthy individuals to fund lavish lifestyles and major investments without reporting taxable earnings. When the asset owner dies, the investments are transferred to heirs with an updated tax basis that erases previous gains. Critics argue this system creates an unfair burden on regular workers who pay taxes on every paycheck. To fix this imbalance, Congress recently introduced legislation like the ROBINHOOD Act to target these asset-backed loans. This proposed law aims to eliminate the loophole by taxing large loans backed by financial portfolios. https://www.gallego.senate.gov/news/press-releases/gallego-introduces-legislation-to-crack-down-on-billionaire-tax-loophole/
